title: Climate Variability Modulates the Impact of Price Spikes on Food Insecurity
abstract: arXiv:2609.24394v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Climate variability influences whether a market disruption escalates into a food crisis, yet broad climate patterns like El Ni\~no, tracked months before they alter hydro-climatic conditions, are still not incorporated as an early-warning component in food-security responses. We address this gap by introducing sensitivity regimes, a stratification of regions by the direction and strength of their vegetation response to the El Ni\~no Southern Oscillation, and using them to estimate how food price spikes affect acute food insecurity across sub-Saharan Africa. Integrating remote sensing, socioeconomic data, and causal machine learning, we find that in regions where ENSO systematically suppresses vegetation, a price spike raises the share of the population at acute risk by 5.4 percentage points in the following month. translated_title: 气候变率调节价格飙升对粮食不安全的影响
translated_abstract: 气候变率决定了一次市场动荡是否会升级为粮食危机，然而像厄尔尼诺这样的大尺度气候模式——在其改变水文气候条件之前数月即可被追踪监测——至今仍未被纳入粮食安全应对行动的早期预警组成部分。我们通过引入“敏感性区制”这一概念来填补这一空白，即根据各地区植被对厄尔尼诺-南方涛动（ENSO）响应的方向和强度对区域进行分层，并利用这些区制来估计粮食价格飙升如何影响撒哈拉以南非洲的急性粮食不安全状况。通过整合遥感数据、社会经济数据和因果机器学习方法，我们发现，在ENSO系统性抑制植被生长的地区，价格飙升会使下个月处于急性风险中的人口比例增加5.4个百分点；而在植被不受ENSO影响或与ENSO呈正相关的地区，估计效应较小（约2个百分点……）
tldr: 该论文创新性地提出“敏感性区制”方法，根据植被对ENSO响应的方向和强度对区域进行分层，结合遥感与因果机器学习发现，在ENSO抑制植被的地区价格飙升会使急性粮食不安全人口比例增加5.4个百分点，从而将厄尔尼诺气候预测纳入粮食安全早期预警体系。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces "sensitivity regimes"—stratifying regions by the direction and strength of vegetation response to ENSO—and using causal machine learning shows that price spikes raise acute food insecurity by 5.4 percentage points in ENSO-suppressed regions, enabling El Niño-based climate forecasts to serve as an early-warning component for food security responses.
